function.description: Simulates the creation of sea foam based on the agitation level of water, amount of organic material, and the presence of salt. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

agitation_level.description: The level of agitation in the water, represented by a scale from 1 (calm) to 10 (very agitated).

organic_material.description: The amount of organic material present in grams per liter. This is a float type value.

salt_presence.description: Indicates whether salt is present (true) or not (false) in the water.

temperature.description: The water temperature in degrees Celsius. If unspecified, defaults to average sea temperature. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The “color” of the ocean isn’t fixed—it’s a mix of physics, biology, and chemistry that changes with location, time, and conditions:

| Factor | Effect on Color |
|--------|----------------|
| **Depth** | Deeper waters absorb longer wavelengths (red/orange), leaving shorter‑wavelength light (blue/green). That’s why open oceans look deep blue. |
| **Water Clarity / Turbidity** | Clear water lets more sunlight penetrate; murky water scatters light differently, often giving a greenish or brown tint. |
| **Phytoplankton & Organic Matter** | High concentrations of phytoplankton reflect green light, turning the surface into a vivid turquoise or even emerald hue. |
| **Sediment & Bottom Type** | Shallow areas over sandy bottoms may appear lighter or yellowish because reflected bottom colors influence what we see above. |
| **Sun Angle & Weather** | Low sun angles at sunrise/sunset scatter short wavelengths less efficiently, producing reds, oranges, pinks—think sunsets over the sea. Overcast skies reduce direct illumination, making the water seem darker or grayer. |

So while many people picture a bright azure or cobalt blue when they think of the sea, its actual appearance ranges from pale teal near shorelines to deep navy in abyssal zones—and it can shift dramatically within minutes depending on weather, biological activity, and your viewpoint.
